decisions.question: How often should another faction's truck pop its smoke dischargers?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.319.0 (row 573): raiders' trucks carry no chemfuel to reload, so a truck of theirs comes loaded for one salvo and pops it the first time it is hit while you are a threat.

options.label: Once a visit
options.detail: As built: one salvo each time it comes to a map

options.label: Every hit, 10 s apart
options.detail: Loaded free each time, as often as yours with the switch on

decisions.why: A real truck carries a few reloads at most; smoke every 10 seconds would blind your guns for the whole fight

decisions.question: Without Combat Extended our ring guns feed from steel. Should steel count as rounds in the ammunition locker?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.319.0 (row 574): a round is whatever a fitted gun's ammunition allows, as Vehicle Framework itself decides, so a gun truck's steel (and the dischargers' chemfuel) goes in the locker.

options.label: Yes, as built
options.detail: Whatever the truck's guns fire counts as rounds

options.label: No, never raw materials
options.detail: Steel and chemfuel stay ordinary cargo; the locker holds only real ammunition items

decisions.why: It is what those guns actually load; without Combat Extended there are no ammunition items, so 'no' would leave the locker empty

decisions.question: Should the turbocharger fitting be refused on an engine that is already turbocharged as built?
decisions.context: Built in Framework 0.320.0 (row 576): a built-in turbo is now a part like a fitted one. The fitting is still offered on those engines and adds its x1.2 on top; if the one turbo part fails, both power losses apply (about 0.58 of rated).

options.label: Refuse it there
options.detail: The Fittings window says the engine already has a turbocharger; any already fitted stays until taken off

options.label: Allow it, as now
options.detail: Read as a bigger turbo on top of the built-in one, with the double loss when it fails

decisions.why: One turbo part stands for one turbo; a second fitting on it has no physical meaning and makes the failure harsher than either alone

decisions.question: Should water tankers and the water bowser exist without Dubs Bad Hygiene, filling from rivers to fight fires?
decisions.context: Your card of 27 Nov 2026 chose 'Both', including river water without Dubs. The card was wrong: it said only the river intake was Dubs-only, but the water itself and the water bowser are too. Without Dubs, water's only use would be fighting fires: the helicopter's bucket and the C-27J's fire tank.

options.label: Bring water to every game
options.detail: Water and the water bowser without Dubs, filling from rivers, lakes or the sea; plumbing and treatment stay with Dubs

options.label: Keep it with Dubs
options.detail: As now: without Dubs, the bucket and the C-27J's tank draw straight from open water

decisions.why: Without Dubs the bucket and the C-27J's tank already draw from open water, so a water bowser would add a vehicle with little to do

decisions.question: Should other factions also help by radio with vehicle repairs, not only medicine?
decisions.context: Built in Radio 0.26.0 (rows 651 to 653): another faction's doctor helps with tending and operations when none of your colonists can. Your card asked for a doctor; the repair and trade kinds were left out.

options.label: Medicine and vehicle repairs
options.detail: A mechanic of theirs talks your mechanic through a repair above their skill, on the same terms

decisions.why: A doctor on the radio is the real thing you described; a faction's mechanic is a stretch, and repairs are rarer and cheaper to wait for

decisions.question: How good should other factions' doctors be?
decisions.context: Built in Radio 0.26.0 as an agent default: Medicine 10 for an industrial faction, 14 for a spacer one, 16 beyond; tribes and medieval factions have no radio and never help.

options.label: 10, 14, 16, as built
options.detail: A solid doctor; lifted halfway, a Medicine 2 carer works at 6
A modest help, so your own doctor still matters more
A specialist on the line: worth building relays for

decisions.why: Good enough to be worth a radio, not so good that a colony never trains its own doctor (the Elmer makes training worth it)

decisions.question: How much goodwill should a neutral faction ask for its doctor's call?
decisions.context: Built in Radio 0.26.0 as an agent default: 3 goodwill a call, a call lasting while used and an hour after, and never taking goodwill below 0, so the help can never turn a faction hostile.

options.label: 3, as built
options.detail: About a fifth of what a small gift buys back
A real price: you would think before calling

decisions.why: Noticeable over a season of calls, cheap for one emergency; the floor at 0 keeps it from ever being a trap

decisions.question: Should a convoy's tends teach the carer when talked through by radio?
decisions.context: Built in Radio 0.26.0 (row 650): the Elmer multiplies the experience the game gives, half again. The game gives no experience for a convoy's tends at all, so on the road the Elmer adds nothing.

options.label: No, as the game
options.detail: On the road nobody learns from tending, as in the unmodded game

options.label: Yes, a little
options.detail: A tend talked through on the road gives the carer some Medicine experience, as a tend at home does

decisions.why: Giving experience the game never gives is a balance change beyond the Elmer; easy to add if you want convoys to train medics
